messages:
alex: Heads-up: after landing the kernel selector optimization (PR #3123) I'm seeing ~+3.1GB resident GPU memory on 8xA100 tensor-parallel runs vs baseline. Throughput and mean latency unchanged, but resident memory spikes.
maria: yikes. only on TP runs? single-GPU ok?
alex: single-GPU looks fine. happens when tensor-split + all-reduce path is active. quick profiler excerpt below:
```
Device 0 resident: 32.7GB
Device 1 resident: 32.9GB
Collective temp allocations (per-device): ~3.2GB
Allocator fragmentation: ~800MB
Top consumers: ncclCollectives -> p2p buffers, runtime workspace
```
cheng: can you repro with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and try toggling NCCL_P2P_DISABLE? might be pooling interaction.
alex: did that. `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` drops resident by ~2.4GB on the same run. so NCCL p2p buffers + our per-stream workspace reservation look like the culprit.
julian: hunch: we're reserving workspace per-stream/shard, so if TP has N shards we multiply the transient workspace. consider switching to a per-device shared workspace to de-dup buffers.
rachel: that could introduce contention. under sustained qps does it increase tail latency?
alex: quick microbench: switch to shared per-device workspace -> resident -2.6GB, 99p latency +3.8ms at 500qps. tradeoff seems acceptable for canary.
maria: plus we should add an allocator hook to free kernel temp buffers immediately after kernel completes so they don't linger in the pool.
cheng: agree. need to be careful with `cudaFreeAsync` semantics and stream sync. maybe keep cudaMallocAsync but return big ephemeral blocks to a fast recycle list keyed by device+stream-epoch.
julian: also explore a small NCCL comm-buffer pool keyed by (device, comm-size) so consecutive all-reduces reuse a single buffer instead of re-allocating per-op.
alex: plan:
- hotfix: switch reserve -> per-device shared workspace (canary)
- implement allocator quick-recycle hook for ephemeral buffers
- experiment: small NCCL comm-buffer pool
I'll open PRs and schedule staging canary.
oncall-bot: deploy-note: canary-1805 scheduled to 3 staging nodes for afternoon smoke tests.
rachel: add a regression alert: resident-GPU > +1.5GB for 8-gpu TP baseline -> fire pager and block rollouts.
alex: will add NVTX ranges and heap snapshots to the PR so perf tests capture details. also adding a microbench harness comparing per-device vs per-stream reserve.
maria: thanks — assigning to alex + cheng. ping me once the canary perf numbers land.
